operating_decision.why: at p@1000 the forest led the ML-07 rule on 5/5 held-out client folds; at p@50 on 4/5. The advantage is consistent at depth, so the queue is built for depth
operating_decision.cost_accepted: a forest cannot explain a row, so reason codes are supplied by the ML-07 rule -- a different scorer than the one that ranked the page
operating_decision.scoring: out-of-fold; every page scored by a forest that never saw its client

archetypes.purpose: the queue says which page next; the archetype says what kind of edit to consider. Triage only -- no refresh outcome exists in this data, so no archetype carries evidence that its action recovers traffic
archetypes.assignment: mutually exclusive, exhaustive, first match wins down the order below
archetypes.tie_break_principle: cheapest and most reversible edit first, so a page that is both a snippet problem and a consolidation candidate is offered the title rewrite

snippet_gap.rationale: ranks on page one and is seen, but clicked less than its position peers: the listing is the likeliest defect, not the body

thin_with_demand.rationale: measured thin against measured demand: add substance before anything else

stale_authority.rationale: a strong, visible page that has not been touched in 90+ days: defend it

deep_but_substantial.rationale: length is not the problem and it ranks deep anyway: question the target query, or merge it into a stronger page

weak_engagement.rationale: people arrive and do not engage: the defect is on the page, above the fold

low_demand.rationale: not obviously defective, but the demand is not there. Editing is the wrong lever and this is where review effort is most often wasted

insufficient_page_data.rationale: word count is missing, so the thin and substantial tests could not run: diagnose the data before diagnosing the page

no_clear_defect.rationale: the model ranks it and none of the above explains why. A human looks, and this residual is reported rather than hidden

archetypes.action_is_not_automated: an archetype selects the review question, never the edit. Every action in this table is performed by a human under the section 3 gate

content_decay.finding: the declining label fires more often on younger pages, not older ones: 0.673 in the (89.0, 120.0] day band against 0.439 in the (470.0, inf] band

refresh_recency_is_nearly_two_valued.why_it_matters: refresh recency cannot be read as a continuous signal here, so this data cannot support a refresh *cadence* recommendation and none is made

interpretation.mechanism_1_post_launch_settling: the prior 30-day window of a young page catches more of its launch ramp. Median prev-30d share falls from 0.342 to 0.305 across the age range while the last-30d share rises. A page settling off a launch spike registers as declining under a label that only compares two adjacent windows
interpretation.mechanism_2_survivorship: ML-09 established the corpus is 100% active content. Pages that launched and died are already gone, so the old bands contain only what stabilised. Some of the attenuation with age is selection and this data cannot separate the two
interpretation.what_this_does_not_license: no claim that content stops decaying with age, and no refresh cadence. Both mechanisms predict the same curve and neither is testable without dated history and refresh outcomes
interpretation.what_it_does_license: read the queue within an age band. Ranked across the whole corpus, the youngest band supplies more of the queue than its share of the corpus, and some of those rows are settling rather than declining

explainability.finding: the ML-07 rule explains only about half of what the forest ranks: the rule fires on thinness, staleness and weak CTR, while the forest ranks on sustained visibility and age, which the rule has no code for

monitoring_triggers.principle: ML-09 measured a fold-to-fold spread of +/-0.054 on precision@1000. Anything inside that band is fold noise; the triggers below sit outside it.

triggers.name: queue_precision_decay
triggers.watch: share of the delivered top-1000 that a reviewer confirms as declining
triggers.rationale: two fold-standard-deviations below what this queue actually delivers. The +/-0.054 comes from ML-09's precision@1000 spread across held-out clients and is used only as the noise scale -- the 0.726 mean it came from is NOT this number and the two are not comparable (see the notebook's section 1 note on denominators)
triggers.action: retrain; if it does not recover, fall back to the ML-07 rule

triggers.name: base_rate_shift
triggers.rationale: +/-0.10 around the 0.542 the model was fitted at; the queue's lift is quoted against that base rate and stops meaning the same thing if it moves
triggers.action: re-quote every lift figure before reusing it; retrain

triggers.name: label_definition_change
triggers.watch: the +/-20% cut on the 30d-vs-prev-30d impression change
triggers.trigger_on: any change to the threshold, the window, or the metric
triggers.rationale: ML-09 found the shipped cut is -20% while the paper documents -10%. A silent change to either would move the label under the model with no error anywhere
triggers.action: stop; re-derive the label, re-run ML-09's reconstruction check, retrain

triggers.name: feature_drift
triggers.watch: median of the forest's top four features
triggers.trigger_on: any median moving more than 25% from the value above
triggers.rationale: these four carry ~45% of importance; the rest barely matter
triggers.action: investigate the source before retraining -- drift here is often a collection change, not a content change

triggers.name: explainability_gap
triggers.watch: share of delivered rows carrying at least one ML-07 rule code
triggers.rationale: the rule already explains only about half the queue, which is why model-derived codes exist. The trigger sits below today's measured coverage, not at an aspirational 0.80 -- a threshold already breached on the day it ships is not a monitor. Total coverage must stay at 1.00 and is asserted in code, not monitored
triggers.action: if rule coverage falls further, the queue is drifting away from what the hand rule was built for -- revisit the rule before the model

triggers.name: queue_concentration
triggers.watch: largest single client's share of the delivered queue
triggers.rationale: per-client declining rates run 0.000 to 0.937, so a queue dominated by one client is measuring that client, not the portfolio
triggers.action: cap per client and re-rank within client
